subject: automotive-technology
intro: Automotive technology leads into the workshops and bays where vehicles are diagnosed, repaired and made safe again — and into the estimating and claims side of the industry that depends on people who understand the machine.

roles.title: Automotive Service Technicians and Mechanics
roles.what: Diagnose, adjust, repair and overhaul cars and light trucks: find the fault from the symptom, replace or rebuild the worn parts, and verify the vehicle leaves safe and roadworthy.
roles.where: Every ASE-area unit maps to a bay — engine repair, electrical diagnostics with wiring diagrams, sensors and ECUs, brakes, steering and suspension, and the emissions, ADAS and EV-high-voltage topics of unit 6.

roles.title: Automotive Body and Related Repairers
roles.what: Repair and refinish vehicle bodies and straighten frames after collisions, restoring panels, structure and finish so the car looks and performs as it did before the damage.
roles.where: Unit 1's shop safety, lifting and service information systems, plus unit 4's knowledge of steering geometry and suspension, ground the structural alignment work collision repair depends on.

roles.title: Bus and Truck Mechanics and Diesel Engine Specialists
roles.what: Diagnose, adjust, repair or overhaul buses and trucks, and maintain and repair diesel engines of every kind, keeping freight and passenger fleets moving.
roles.where: Unit 2's four-stroke operation and engine diagnosis, unit 5's drivetrains and transmissions, and unit 6's emissions control and testing extend directly to the heavier compression-ignition engines of fleet work.

roles.title: Insurance Appraisers, Auto Damage
roles.what: Appraise vehicle damage to determine repair costs for insurance claim settlement, preparing cost estimates and agreeing figures with repair shops.
roles.where: Unit 4's brakes, steering and suspension knowledge and unit 3's electrical diagnostics let you judge what collision damage really costs, with unit 1's service information systems as the estimating reference.
